items.userText:
Extend the supplied SyncWise computational system for an optical fabric.
Work in /workspace with Python3.11, NumPy2.3.5 and NetworkX3.6.1.
Read PROTOCOL.md, MODEL.md, CERTIFICATES.md and TRACE.md for the full contract.
Implement submission/main.py; additional Python modules may live in submission/.
Read JSON requests from stdin and flush one JSON response per request.
Support calibrate, plan, audit and replay with the published schemas.
Infer tight port-bias ranges from noisy relative-delay constraints.
Choose the smallest safe hardware guard setting and provide a checkable certificate.
Account for sampled circuits, delayed application, heating and periodic references.
Audit certificates independently of their choice of optimal witness paths.
Replay packet losses, competing transmissions and clock-incarnation changes exactly.
Preserve integer precision, unknown clocks and the stated boundary conventions.
Legacy stochastic APIs are retained; the new exact model hooks are incomplete.
Only the bounded regular-file submission tree is collected for offline execution.
All required packages are installed; no optical hardware or network is needed.
Run python3 public_check.py for the small public-only sanity check.
Passing that check does not establish correctness over the published domain.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
The implementation is complete. Summary of what was built in `/workspace/submission/`:

**`main.py`** — JSONL driver: reads one request per line, dispatches `calibrate`/`plan`/`audit`/`replay`, flushes one JSON response per request.

**`para.py`** (calibration hooks) — Exact integer calibration:
- Measurements become a difference-constraint graph (constraint ids `2i` upper, `2i+1` lower); feasibility is decided by Bellman–Ford, and inconsistency yields a *genuine* negative cycle (1-based ids, chained in traversal order).
- Tight suprema `U[a][b]` = shortest-path distances, with per-source shortest-path *trees* (Johnson-reweighted Dijkstra) supplying checkable witness constraint ids.
- Minimax centre `c` and worst residual, exactly in attoseconds (half-ps cases stay integral), plus the calibrated hop allowance `H`.

**`topo.py`** (calendar) — Declared period `P = Q·S/gcd(T,Q·S)`, per-phase slice/rho, effective drift rates (base + additive heat), per-phase anchors, per-link blackout phase masks, and per-phase directed transfers with the exact receiver-ageing allowance (prefix-summed, integer-exact).

**`algo.py`** (planning/audit) — Lexicographic `(bound, age)` Dijkstra over the phase-device graph (waiting intervals + eligible transfers), per-guard peaks, smallest safe guard (`g·1000 ≥ peak + reconfig·1000`), exact envelope/age matrices, attaining witness predecessors, and the exact warmup cycle; plus an independent auditor that re-derives every scalar, validates calibration feasibility/tightness/witnesses, witness lineage steps, and the certificate inequalities, accepting alternative optimal witnesses.

**`simulator.py`** (clock engine) — Exact packet replay: drift → reboot → anchor → application ordering, generation counters and staleness, unknown payloads, least-bound/smallest-id adoption with strict improvement only, send precedence (`not_in_slice`, `blackout`, `guard`, `port_busy`) with ID service priority, ageing across phases/period wrap, and all counters.

Validation: cross-checked against independent brute-force/reference implementations (envelope, ageing, warmup schedule simulation, replay) on thousands of randomized fabrics/profiles/traces, plus defect-injection tests for the auditor; `python3 public_check.py` passes and the tree meets the published file/size bounds.
